title: Review: Work, energy and power; Rigid body mechanics; Galilean and special relativity; Thermal energy transfers

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Spring constant (k)
items.clue: The force per unit extension for a body obeying Hooke's law.

items.label: Efficiency (η)
items.clue: The fraction of the total input that is transferred usefully.

items.label: Convection current
items.clue: Warm, less dense fluid rises, cools, becomes denser and sinks.

items.label: Black body
items.clue: Absorbs all the radiation falling on it and is the best possible emitter.

questions.stem: A spring of spring constant 180 N m⁻¹ is compressed by 0.10 m and then released to launch a trolley of mass 0.50 kg along a smooth horizontal track. All the elastic potential energy is transferred to the trolley's kinetic energy. What is the speed of the trolley?

options.text: 6.0 m s⁻¹
2.7 m s⁻¹
1.9 m s⁻¹
1.3 m s⁻¹

questions.stem: An electric motor with an efficiency of 0.60 takes an input power of 1.5 kW. It lifts a load of mass 90 kg vertically at constant speed. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the load?
questions.explanation: Useful power out = η × total power in = 0.60 × 1500 = 900 W. At constant speed P = Fv with F = mg = 90 × 9.8 = 882 N, so v = 900 / 882 = 1.02 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: Hydrogen gas at atmospheric pressure releases 120 MJ of energy per kilogram and 0.011 MJ per litre when burned. Petrol releases 46 MJ per kilogram and 34 MJ per litre. Which conclusion is supported by these data?

options.text: A litre of hydrogen releases about 2.6 times the energy of a litre of petrol.
A litre of petrol releases about 3000 times as much energy as a litre of hydrogen.
A kilogram of petrol releases more energy than a kilogram of hydrogen, as petrol is denser.
Hydrogen releases its energy about 2.6 times faster than petrol does when it is burned.

questions.stem: A car of mass 1200 kg starts from rest on a level road. The driving force on it is 4000 N and the total resistive force is 1000 N; both are constant. What is the speed of the car after it has travelled 50 m?
questions.explanation: Resultant force = 4000 − 1000 = 3000 N. Work done by the resultant force = 3000 × 50 = 1.5 × 10⁵ J = ΔE_k = ½ × 1200 × v², so v = √(2 × 1.5 × 10⁵ / 1200) = √250 = 15.8 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A block of mass 0.40 kg hangs from a vertical spring of spring constant 50 N m⁻¹. At one instant the block is moving at 1.5 m s⁻¹, its centre is 0.30 m above the level chosen as the zero of gravitational potential energy, and the spring is stretched by 0.20 m from its natural length. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the mechanical energy of the block–spring–Earth system at this instant?

Blocks of mass 2.0 kg and 4.0 kg are released from rest at the same height. The 2.0 kg block slides down a steep ramp and the 4.0 kg block down a shallow ramp; the bottoms of the two ramps are at the same level. Both ramps are frictionless and air resistance is negligible. How do their speeds at the bottom compare?

options.text: The 4.0 kg block is faster, because its weight is twice as large.
The lighter block is faster, because its steeper ramp gives it more acceleration.
The 4.0 kg block is faster, because it accelerates for longer on its ramp.
They are equal, as each block loses the same potential energy per kilogram.

questions.explanation: With no frictional or resistive forces, mechanical energy is conserved: mgΔh = ½mv², so v = √(2gΔh). Mass cancels and the path shape does not appear, so both blocks reach the same speed.

questions.stem: A student of mass 55 kg climbs a staircase from a platform 4.0 m above the ground to a landing 10.0 m above the ground. The staircase is 12 m long, measured along its slope. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the increase in her gravitational potential energy?
questions.explanation: ΔE_p = mgΔh with Δh = 10.0 − 4.0 = 6.0 m: ΔE_p = 55 × 9.8 × 6.0 = 3234 J ≈ 3.2 × 10³ J. The length of the staircase does not matter; only the vertical change in height does.

questions.stem: Crane X lifts a load through a height of 10 m in 20 s. Crane Y lifts an identical load through the same height in 40 s. Both lift at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: X does twice as much work as Y, because it transfers energy faster.
Both do equal work, and X develops twice as much power as Y.
Y does more work than X, because it applies its force for twice as long.
Both develop the same power, as they exert equal forces on their loads.

questions.explanation: Each crane lifts the same weight through the same height, so each does the same work, mgΔh. Power is the rate of doing work, P = ΔW/Δt; X takes half the time, so it develops twice the power.

questions.stem: A Sankey diagram for a car engine has an input arrow representing 200 kJ of chemical energy from the fuel. It divides into four output arrows: 60 kJ of useful mechanical work, 100 kJ of thermal energy carried away by the exhaust gases, 30 kJ of thermal energy removed by the cooling system, and 10 kJ of sound. What is the efficiency of the engine?
questions.explanation: η = useful work out / total work in = 60 kJ / 200 kJ = 0.30 = 30%.

questions.stem: A coal-fired power station has an electrical power output of 600 MW and an overall efficiency of 0.40. The energy density of the coal it burns is 30 MJ kg⁻¹, that is, each kilogram burned releases 30 MJ. What mass of coal must the station burn each second?

options.text: 20.0 kg s⁻¹
8.00 kg s⁻¹
50.0 kg s⁻¹
33.3 kg s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Total power in = useful power out / η = 600 MW / 0.40 = 1500 MW = 1500 MJ s⁻¹. Mass per second = 1500 MJ s⁻¹ ÷ 30 MJ kg⁻¹ = 50.0 kg s⁻¹.

questions.stem: At 100 °C and atmospheric pressure, liquid water has a density of 958 kg m⁻³ and steam has a density of 0.598 kg m⁻³. What do these data show about the molecules in steam compared with those in the liquid water?

options.text: Their mean separation is about 12 times larger, as the volume per molecule is 1600 times larger.
Their mean separation is about 1600 times larger, because the density is 1600 times smaller.
Each molecule is about 1600 times larger, so each one takes up 1600 times the space.
Each molecule has about 1/1600 of the mass, because a gas is much lighter than a liquid.

questions.stem: The density of aluminium is 2.7 g cm⁻³. What is the volume, in m³, of an aluminium block of mass 0.081 kg?
questions.explanation: ρ = m/V, so V = m/ρ = 81 g/2.7 g cm⁻³ = 30 cm³. Since 1 cm³ = (10⁻² m)³ = 10⁻⁶ m³, V = 30 × 10⁻⁶ m³ = 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ m³. (In SI: V = 0.081 kg/2700 kg m⁻³ gives the same result.)

questions.stem: A rigid body is free to turn about a fixed axis. One of the forces acting on it lies in a plane perpendicular to the axis. Under which condition is the torque of this force about the axis zero?

options.text: It acts perpendicular to the line from the axis to where it acts.
The body remains at rest while this force acts on it.
An equal force acts on the other side, at the same distance.
Its line of action passes through the axis of rotation.

questions.explanation: τ = Fr sin θ. If the line of action passes through the axis, θ = 0° or 180°, so sin θ = 0; equivalently the perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of action is zero.

questions.stem: A rigid body is in rotational equilibrium. Which statement about the body must be true?

options.text: The body is not rotating about any axis.
The forces on each side of its axis are equal.
The resultant torque acting on the body is zero.
The resultant force acting on the body is zero.

questions.explanation: Rotational equilibrium is defined by zero resultant torque, so there is no angular acceleration. The body may be at rest or rotating at a constant angular speed.

questions.stem: A wheel is mounted on a frictionless axle. Starting from rest, a constant resultant torque acts on it for a few seconds and is then removed. How does the wheel move after the torque is removed?

options.text: It keeps rotating at a constant angular speed.
It slows down steadily and then stops rotating.
Its angular speed rises until the torque is used up.
It stops, as its angular acceleration is now zero.

questions.explanation: With no resultant torque there is no angular acceleration (α = τ/I = 0), so the wheel keeps the angular speed it had when the torque was removed. This is the rotational form of Newton's first law.

questions.stem: A rigid disc rotates at a steady rate about a fixed axis through its centre. Point P on the disc is 0.10 m from the axis and point Q is 0.20 m from the axis. How do the motions of P and Q compare?

options.text: Q has twice the angular velocity and twice the linear speed.
Both have the same angular velocity and the same linear speed.
Same angular velocity; Q has twice the linear speed of P.
Q has half the angular velocity of P, because ω = v/r.

questions.explanation: Every point of a rigid body turns through the same angle in the same time, so P and Q share one angular velocity. Linear speed v = ωr, so Q, at twice the distance, has twice the linear speed.

questions.stem: A wheel starts from rest and turns with a uniform angular acceleration of 3.0 rad s⁻². What is its angular speed at the moment it completes 8.0 revolutions?

options.text: 6.93 rad s⁻¹
12.3 rad s⁻¹
8.68 rad s⁻¹
17.4 rad s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Δθ = 8.0 × 2π = 50.3 rad. ω_f² = ω_i² + 2αΔθ = 0 + 2 × 3.0 × 50.3 = 302 rad² s⁻², so ω_f = 17.4 rad s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of mass M and length L can rotate either about an axis through its centre (I = ML²/12) or about an axis through one end (I = ML²/3), both perpendicular to the rod. The same resultant torque acts in each case. What is the ratio (angular acceleration about the centre)/(angular acceleration about the end)?
questions.explanation: α = τ/I and τ is the same, so α_centre/α_end = I_end/I_centre = (ML²/3)/(ML²/12) = 4.00. Rotating about the centre puts the mass closer to the axis, so I is smaller and α larger.
